chunks: The mention of the affair of Abul Hasan Ali bin Muhammad al-Samarrani after Shaykh Abul Qasim al-Husayn bin Ruh, may Allah be pleased with him,
and the severing of the signs through him, and they are the Four Doors:

key_terms.السَّمُرِّيِّ: Al-Samarrani (a nisba indicating origin from Samarra)
key_terms.الْأَبْوَابُ: The Doors (referring to the four special deputies)
key_terms.الْأَعْلَامِ: The signs/standards (referring to the deputies who were the primary signs of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who succeeded Abul Qasim bin Ruh as the deputy of the Imam and what does the term 'Al-Abwab' refer to?
ai.summary: This passage marks the conclusion of the era of the 'Four Doors' (al-Abwab) by introducing Abul Hasan Ali bin Muhammad al-Samari as the final special deputy of Imam al-Mahdi (aj). His subsequent disappearance (ghayat al-khabar) signifies the transition from special deputyship (al-Imama al-Khassa) to general deputyship (al-Imama al-Amma), a pivotal moment in Twelver Shia eschatology that establishes the framework for the Imam's occultation until the present day.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: After Shaykh Abul Qasim Husain bin Rauh, Abul Hasan Ali bin Muhammad Saymoori succeeded to the post of the deputyship of Imam Mahdi (a.s)
and with his death ended the special deputyship of Imam (a.s). Only these four were channels of contact with the Imam of the Time (a.s).
